turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — lovely to hear from you. How's your day been treating you so far?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Oh. Not really. Just tired, I suppose.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, one of those mornings then. Biscuit been keeping you company at least, or is he off doing his own thing?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …On the chair. Asleep, as usual.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Classic cat — claim the best seat and clock off. Has he got a favourite chair, or does he just pinch whichever one's warmest?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The armchair. He claims it and won't move.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ah, so you've lost the armchair to a fluffy landlord — fair enough. Do you end up on the sofa yourself, then, or do you negotiate?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The sofa. I don't fight him. Not worth it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Wise choice — cats always win those negotiations anyway. Have you had a cup of tea yet this morning, or still working up to it?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Had a cup. Didn't fancy the crossword.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, tea without the puzzle — fair enough, some mornings the clues can wait. What do you usually go for instead when you're not in a crossword mood?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Nothing, really. Just sit there. Can't be bothered.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm… sitting with a warm cup is its own thing sometimes. Tea or coffee person, usually — or are you firmly a tea house?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Tea. Proper tea, always. Coffee's not for me.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Proper tea — I'm with you there; if I had a kettle I'd be a builder's-tea type myself. Milk and one sugar, or do you take it plain?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Milk, one sugar. Strong brew, proper strong.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Strong brew with milk and one — that's a proper cup. Do you have a favourite biscuit to go with it, or is tea better on its own?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Digestives, usually. Haven't bothered lately, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Digestives are classic — nothing fancy needed. Speaking of ordinary comforts, what's the weather like your way today?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Grey and wet. Same as always.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ah, that grey drizzle that never quite decides. Perfect excuse for staying indoors with the telly — anything you've been watching lately?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Nothing. Nothing's on worth watching.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, the schedules can be a bit thin. What about radio — do you ever put that on in the background?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Sometimes. Can't be bothered changing it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, leaving it on whatever's there is fair enough. Tell me — what was your favourite subject to teach, back when you were in the classroom?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …History. The children liked the stories.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: History with stories — that sounds like a lovely way into it. What kind of stories did the children get stuck into most?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Castles, mostly. The Romans did well too.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Castles and Romans — hard to beat that for a primary class. Did you ever take them on a trip to see a real castle?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Once or twice. Caerphilly, I think — they loved it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Caerphilly — what a place for a school trip; I can imagine them tearing about the walls. What do you remember most from that day?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The rain, mostly. And them tearing about the battlements.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Rain and battlements — a proper Welsh school outing then. Do you still like wandering round old places yourself, or was that more a teaching thing?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Used to. Can't be bothered now, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, fair enough — those days had their own rhythm. What about cooking — do you still like making a proper meal, or is it more toast and whatever's easy?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …More toast, these days. Can't be bothered cooking.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Toast has its place — no shame in that. What did you used to make for Sunday dinner, back when you were cooking more?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Roast, with all the trimmings. The good plates came out.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A proper roast with the good plates — that sounds like a proper Sunday. Was it always beef, or did you ring the changes with chicken or lamb?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Beef, mostly. Chicken when Siobhan came.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Beef for the usual Sundays, chicken when Siobhan was home — nice little tradition. Does she still have a favourite pudding from those days?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Sticky toffee. She'd fight you for the last bit.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Sticky toffee — I'd fight for the last bit too if I could eat. Do you still make it now and then, or is it more a memory these days?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Memory, really. Can't be bothered now.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, memories keep well enough on their own. Cats or dogs — and don't say Biscuit counts as both — which way do you lean?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Cats. Biscuit's enough for one person.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Cats it is — I'm fond of a soft collie myself, but Biscuit's clearly got the job covered. How long have you had him now?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Three years, this month. Tom picked him out.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Three years this month — and Tom picked him out. That must make Biscuit rather special. What was it about him that caught Tom's eye?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Scrawny little thing. Tom said he'd keep us company.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A scrawny little thing who was meant to keep you company — Tom had good instincts there. Does Biscuit still have that skinny look, or has he filled out on armchair life?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Fat, now. Filled out on the armchair life, like you say.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! From scrawny to plump landlord — success, in cat terms. What's his favourite treat these days, if he still gets them?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Salmon pouches. He knows the packet, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Salmon pouches — and he knows the packet; that's a clever old boy. Have you got any plants or a little garden going at the moment?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …A few roses. Haven't touched them in a while.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Roses are forgiving things, often enough. What colour are yours — the classic reds, or something softer?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Red, mostly. One pink that never behaves itself.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! A pink that won't behave — every garden needs a troublemaker. Does it sprawl, or just flower at the wrong time?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Both, really. Sprawls and flowers whenever it likes.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sprawls and flowers on its own schedule — fair play to it. If you could be anywhere warm right now, where would you go?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Spain, maybe. Somewhere by the sea. We never got there.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Spain by the sea — that does sound lovely. I'm sorry you never quite made it; what was it about the place that appealed?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The light, mostly. And being somewhere different.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The light, and a change of scene — that makes sense. Have you ever been somewhere that did feel properly different, even for a short trip?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Scotland, once. All that rain — same as here.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! All that rain — so not quite the sunshine holiday. Was there anything you did like about Scotland despite the weather?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The hills, I suppose. Even in the rain.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The hills even in the rain — that says a lot. What's the best thing you've read lately, if you've had a book on the go?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Halfway through one. Can't seem to get through it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, some books just sit there half-finished. What's this one about, if you don't mind saying?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …One of those murder stories. Can't remember the names, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A murder story — I like those for the puzzle of it. Do you usually go for the cosy village ones, or the darker city sort?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Village ones, mostly. Darker ones are a bit much, some days.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Village ones — quieter trouble, somehow. Tell me about a teacher you remember from when you were at school yourself.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Miss Hartley, my first teacher. Strict, but kind underneath.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Miss Hartley — strict with kindness underneath is a good combination. What made you notice the kind bit?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …She'd wait at the door for the slow ones. I noticed that.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Waiting at the door for the slow ones — that says a lot about her. Do you think you carried a bit of that into your own teaching?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …I hope so. I tried to, anyway.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Trying counts — and the children who liked your history stories suggest you managed it. What's your favourite breed of dog, even as a cat person?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Collies, I think. Gentle things.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Collies — we're agreed then; gentle and clever. Did you ever have a dog growing up, or was it always cats in the house?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Blackie, a lab. Best dog I ever had.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Blackie the lab — best dog you ever had; that's a high bar. What was he like around the house?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …A great soft lump. Slept by the fire all day.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A great soft lump by the fire — sounds perfect, really. Do you still keep a fire going much, or is it more radiators these days?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Rarely. Can't be bothered with the fiddling.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, fires do take a bit of fiddling. Have you got anything planned for the rest of the day, or is it a quiet one?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Nothing, really. Maybe the shops, if I feel like it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Maybe the shops if the mood takes you — fair enough. What's usually on the list when you do go?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Milk, bread, the cat's food. The usual.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Milk, bread, and Biscuit's supplies — the essentials sorted. Do you have a corner shop nearby, or is it a bit of a trek to the supermarket?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The Co-op, mostly. A bit of a walk, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The Co-op on a bit of a walk — that can clear the head if the weather behaves. Do you bump into anyone you know when you're there?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Not really. Keep myself to myself, these days.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, keeping to yourself is fine. What about music — do you ever put a record or the radio on for a bit of company?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Radio, mostly. Records are too much fiddling.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Radio's easier — leave it on and let it do the work. What's usually playing when you've got it going?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Radio 4, mostly. Whatever's on, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Radio 4 — good company in the background. Do you prefer the plays, or more the chat and the news?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The chat, mostly. Plays take too much following.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Chat you can dip in and out of — makes sense. What was your favourite thing to do on a Saturday when you were still teaching?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The market, Saturdays. Bread and cheese, mostly.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Market Saturdays for bread and cheese — that sounds like a nice rhythm. Do you still get there now and then, or has that slipped a bit?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Slipped, I think. Only when I feel up to it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, when you feel up to it is fair. Are you more of a sweet or savoury breakfast person — toast with jam, or something else?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Savoury, mostly. Egg on toast, if I'm bothered.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Egg on toast — solid choice; if I cooked I'd be a scrambled person myself. Soft-boiled or fried when you do have it?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Fried. Can't be bothered with soft ones.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Fried it is — less fuss than watching a timer. What about the garden birds — do you get any visitors at the window?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Pigeons, mostly. They take the table over.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Pigeons claiming the table — another set of landlords. Does Biscuit watch them from the window, or has he given up?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Watches them a bit. Falls asleep on the sill.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Watches a bit then conks out on the sill — very Biscuit. Does Siobhan still ring on Sundays, or has the timing shifted a bit?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Same as always, Sundays. She rings.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sundays, same as always — nice to have that fixed point. What do you two usually chat about when she rings?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The grandchildren, mostly. School news and all that.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Grandchildren and school news — that must keep you in the loop. How many have you got now?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Two. Ella and Rory, in Dublin.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ella and Rory in Dublin — nice pair of names. What ages are they these days?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Eight and five, I think. Ella's the serious one.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Eight and five, and Ella's the serious one — so Rory's the chatterbox, is he?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …He talks a lot, mind. Ella just listens.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Him talking, her listening — a proper little pair. When did you last see them in person?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Christmas, I think. A few days, it was.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Christmas for a few days — that must have been busy and lovely. What was the nicest bit of having them in the house?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Ella reading to Biscuit. She does that every visit.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ella reading to Biscuit every visit — that's a lovely little tradition. Does he sit still for it, or wander off halfway through?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Half listens, I'd say. Folds up on her lap.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Half listening and folded on her lap — that's as good as applause from a cat. What's something you're looking forward to, even a little thing?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Siobhan ringing Sunday. That's about it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Siobhan on Sunday — that's a solid thing to have marked. Do you prefer mornings for a chat, or afternoon when the day's settled a bit?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Afternoon. Mornings are slow to get going.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Afternoon suits a slow morning — fair enough. What was your favourite subject when you were a schoolgirl yourself?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …English, I think. I liked the stories.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: English for the stories — that tracks, given how you taught history. Was there a book from those days you still remember fondly?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The Railway Children. Read it twice, I think.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The Railway Children twice — that's a book that sticks. What was it about it that made you go back for a second go?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Just liked it. The steam, the girls being brave.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The steam and the girls being brave — that's a lovely reason to read it twice. Do you still like a bit of sewing or knitting, or was that never your thing?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Knitting, a bit. Half-finished things, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Half-finished knitting — I've heard that's the true mark of a knitter. What were you working on last, if you remember?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …A scarf, I think. Still sitting on the needles.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A scarf still on the needles — it'll wait patiently enough. What colour yarn did you choose for it?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Grey, I think. Can't be bothered to look, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Grey's a good everyday colour for a scarf. What's the view like from your window on a day like this?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The garden, mostly. The street beyond it. Nothing much.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Garden and the street beyond — quiet enough. Do you get many neighbours walking past, or is it a still sort of road?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Not many, mind. Everybody keeps to themselves.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, a keep-to-themselves kind of street. Do you like a bit of football on the telly, or never been your sport?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Not really. Never was my sport.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Fair enough — not everyone's game. What about baking — did you ever do much of that, cakes and such?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Cakes, once. Can't be bothered now, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, cakes for another time then. What was your go-to cake when you did bake — Victoria sponge, or something else?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Victoria sponge, mostly. Nothing fancy.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Victoria sponge, nothing fancy — sometimes that's the best sort. Jam and cream in the middle, or just jam?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Jam always. Cream when I could be bothered.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Jam always, cream when the mood struck — solid policy. Have you got a favourite season, or do they all blend a bit?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Autumn, I think. The garden goes quiet.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Autumn when the garden goes quiet — that has a certain peace to it. Do you like the smell of leaves, or is it more the cooler evenings?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Cooler evenings, mostly. Leaves are a bother to rake.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Cooler evenings without the raking — fair trade. What's something you're proud of, looking back — teaching or otherwise?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The kids, I suppose. Some of them wrote after I left.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Some of them writing after you left — that says you mattered to them. What did they tend to say, if you remember?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …That they'd liked history. One still remembers the castles.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Someone still remembering the castles — that's a proper legacy for a history teacher. Do you keep any of those letters, or did they go in a drawer somewhere?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …A drawer somewhere, I think. Somewhere safe.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Somewhere safe in a drawer — good place for them. What about board games — ever play anything with Siobhan or the grandchildren?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Scrabble, sometimes. Ella beats me at it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Ella beating you at Scrabble at eight — serious and sharp with words. Do you let her win, or does she earn it fair and square?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Fair and square. She's sharp, mind you.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Fair and square and sharp — good for her. Do you prefer soup or a sandwich when lunch is just for you?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Sandwich, mostly. Can't be bothered with soup.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sandwich wins for ease — no stirring required. Cheese, or something else when you make one?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Cheese, mostly. Or ham, if I'm feeling posh.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Cheese for ordinary days, ham when you're feeling posh — ha! Do you still write letters by hand, or is it all phone now?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Used to. Don't bother now, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, phones are quicker. What's the nicest place you've ever lived, if you think back?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …This house, I suppose. We did it up together.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: This house that you did up together — that makes it special. What was the first thing you sorted when you moved in?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The beds, I think. Then the garden, come spring.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Beds first, garden come spring — sensible order. Was the garden mostly roses from the start, or did that come later?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Tom did the roses. I did the vegetables, once.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Tom on the roses, you on the vegetables — nice split. What did you grow when you were doing the veg?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Runner beans and potatoes. Nothing fancy.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Runner beans and potatoes — proper useful crops. Do you miss digging about in the veg patch, or was it more hard work than pleasure?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Miss it, I suppose. Can't be bothered now.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, missing it and leaving it be can sit together. What's the best cuppa you've ever had — anywhere at all?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Here, honestly. This kitchen, this mug.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: This kitchen and this mug — that's a lovely answer. Is it a particular mug, or just whichever's clean?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The green one. Tom picked it out, years ago.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The green one Tom picked — that makes the tea taste better somehow. Do you still have a favourite chair for drinking it in, even if Biscuit steals the armchair?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The green one by the window. Biscuit's on it now.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Even the green window chair isn't safe — he's thorough. Do you end up standing with your tea sometimes, or claim the sofa again?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Sofa again. Same as always.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sofa again, same as always — at least it's soft. Have you got any photos up around the house that you like looking at?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The grandchildren, mostly. And Tom, on the mantel.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Grandchildren and Tom on the mantel — good company to have there. Is there a particular photo of him you like best?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …One in the garden, laughing. Don't know why I like that one.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Him laughing in the garden — you don't always need a why for that. What was he laughing at, if you remember the day?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Biscuit chasing a pigeon, I think. He never did catch one.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ha! Biscuit never catching the pigeon — classic. What's the weather doing out there now — still grey, or brightened a touch?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Still grey. Rain's stopped, I think.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Grey but the rain's eased — small mercies. Do you fancy a walk if it holds, or happier staying put today?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Happier staying put. Knee's playing up today.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'm sorry — a playing-up knee is a nuisance. Staying put sounds wise then. Has it been bothering you much this week?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …On and off. Doesn't help the sleeping, mind.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, that does sound rough — pain and poor sleep feeding each other. Have you got a comfy spot on the sofa for resting it today?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Sofa end, near the lamp. That's my spot.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sofa end by the lamp — that's a proper claim. Do you keep a book there for dipping into, even if progress is slow?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …The murder one. Still sitting there, half-done.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still sitting there half-done — no rush with a village mystery. What about jigsaws — ever do those on a rainy afternoon?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Used to. Too much fiddling now.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mm, lots of little pieces to keep track of. Are you more of a morning person or an evening person these days?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Evening, these days. Mornings are slow.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Evening person with slow mornings — that tracks. What's your favourite thing about evenings at home?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …Radio, tea, the lamp on. That's about it.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
